pairs.why: The two are almost the same, but A's silver faceplate and lenses are slightly softer and more matte, and B's lenses look a little more glassy and polished.
A is busier and more saturated, with mirror-like lenses, a toy-like bolted base and extra props; B keeps the calmer blue-and-silver finish and simple framing of the real card.
A's hooded, goggle-eyed head is more cartoon-toy and glossier; B is calmer, though its large silver face is still a different build from the real horizontal housing.
A is a chunky, glossy toy with oversized seeds; B's thinner wooden build, plank roof and rope tied to the roof ends read more like the real feeder.
A's rope ties to the roof ends and its simple plank build match the real feeder; B adds metal rings and arched cut-outs the real card lacks.
B hangs from a metal bracket and has visible screws and an open gable, which reads more as a manufactured object; A's rope-hung plank feeder is closer to the real card.
A's keys are blank, so it isn't built like a working calculator; B has labelled number keys and cyan operator keys like the real card, though its number keys are white instead of dark blue.
A again has blank keys; B has proper labelled number keys and cyan operator keys like the real calculator, though its number keys are pale instead of navy.
